# Supported scope

Target: bpf-mlir `v1.21.0` (commit 41b18856). The tables follow what the ebpf-compile of this version accepts and rejects.

Evidence and status per feature group. **Status**: **supported** = frontend negative examples + a differential or selftest run on 3 kernels (7.1.8 / 6.12.111 / 6.6.157) + a row in the non-root capability matrix; if any of these is missing, **limited** (naming what is missing). Negative examples and example packages are generated from the frontend's analysis; status and limits are maintained by hand, and tests check the evidence behind each status and that the status agrees with the generated columns. The limits and notes of each group are in one place in [notes.md](notes.md).

| G01 | — | **no limits** |

| G03 | — | **no limits** |
| G04 | "Direction of fexit signature errors" | only the retsig check before load guards against a wrong signature (nargs, width, sign) — LoadUnchecked does not check it |
| G05 | "kprobe" | a pointer argument is only the value `uint64(bpf.KprobeArg[uintptr](ctx, n))` (not dereferenced — there is no read through it; only do_sys_poll's ufds was measured)<br>for functions with a compiler suffix (.isra / .part etc.), only programs that do not read arguments under the suffixed name (the number of .part copies differs from the number of calls in the source) |
| G06 | "uprobe" | C++ targets are not measured (the DW_AT_language table accepts the C++ family)<br>does not fire at inlined calls<br>a non-root loader needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN (measured passing on 3 kernels with the set bpf,perfmon,sys_admin — the need is a kernel condition)<br>the file offset error "vaddr as the offset" (st_value − p_vaddr + p_offset) is hidden by fixtures with p_vaddr = p_offset; a non-PIE binary (difference 0x400000) catches it by kernel refusal (the offset is outside the file), and a fixture with a 0x1000 difference (the offset is inside the file) catches it by differential values (a silently different address — no events) |
| G07 | "Kernel 6.6 and the walk unroll count" | on 6.6 kernels, walk unroll counts N > 16 make the verifier's processed count jump |
| G08 | "Packet rewriting" | **no limits** |
| G09 | — | **no limits** |
| G10 | "devmap and redirect_map" | the result is the requested action, not delivery success (a veth without GRO / XDP on the receiving side does not deliver) |
| G11 | "Tail calls" | **no limits** |
| G12 | — | **no limits** |
| G13 | — | **no limits** |
| G14 | — | **no limits** |
| G15 | — | **no limits** |
| G16 | — | **no limits** |
| G17 | "lpm_trie" | **no limits** |
| G18 | "Global variables" | **no limits** |
| G19 | "Stack traces and perf events" | user stacks are walked with frame pointers only — a target without frame pointers gives depth 1 or bogus frames (which can also look like frames outside r-x or build ID status 1)<br>frames of binaries linked by Go's internal linker have build ID status 2 (the note is outside PT_NOTE); user stacks of a uprobe in the middle of a function are not measured |
| G20 | "Stack traces and perf events" | simultaneous overflow on several CPUs is not measured (one CPU and one page only) |
| G21 | "Spin locks and timers" | lock contention under a real packet attach is only the example's single run on lo (the differential uses test runs) |
| G22 | "Spin locks and timers" | no restart from the program side (a second Init returns −EBUSY) — a periodic timer is a Start of its own timer inside the callback (G78)<br>many elements and a series of short deadlines are not measured |
| G23 | "Loop unroll estimate" | a loop without a directive is always unrolled ((U), N ≤ 64) — a back-edge loop is `//gobpf:loop backedge` (G52) |
| G24 | "Calls inside loops" | moving a body into a function does not necessarily reduce the verifier's cost (the ratio of verified instructions, callee / inline, ranged from 0.79 to 3.0 by shape and kernel). The only effect is avoiding the (U) estimate limit of 4096 |
| G31 | "Subprogram borrowed arguments and global subprograms" | **a global borrowed argument (arg:nonnull) is stopped by the target check's arg_tag on 6.6.157** (an expected refusal). static, integer-only global, and maybe_ref global subprograms pass on 6.6<br>at most one borrowed argument, no forwarding to another subprogram. Writes to a borrowed argument (field stores, ++ / op=, bpf.AtomicAdd) are accepted — a non-atomic RMW of a shared map value is GB028 / GB021 at the call site (from the callee's summary). The write differential (field stores, AtomicAdd, per-CPU ++ / +=, maybe_ref, window and borrow) matches the model on 3 kernels as root, a callee's AtomicAdd under multi-CPU concurrency loses no counts, and the non-root matrix has the item cwrite. An integer-value `*p = v` is not accepted, as in programs. Context arguments are G34, packet-window arguments G32<br>the cost of a global also grows with the number of calls (the slope is about half that of static). A callee relying on the caller's range cannot be written (GB006), so a global losing range information does not occur |
| G32 | "Subprogram packet-window arguments" | the length is the same Check n at every call site (part of the window type — bpf-mlir does not shrink it either). A helper has no ctx — nested Checks happen in the caller (longest first)<br>a writing helper is allowed only when every calling program is xdp (GB013 — bpf-mlir also names it at compile time). One window, and forwarding is stopped by gobpf (bpf-mlir accepts it — to be relaxed on demand). One window together with one map-value pointer is accepted<br>test runs do not accept frames shorter than 14 bytes (tc IPv4 34, IPv6 54) — classifying frames under 14 bytes is not run. The verified instruction count can grow with the helper shape (+24 to 30% in tccount) |
| G33 | "Known limitations" | depth is at most 2 (a third is GB001). A second borrow that may point to the same value (a variable key of the same map, the same constant key, a map with the same value type as a borrowed argument) is GB029 — bpf-mlir accepts it (only the frontend is stricter)<br>a borrow from outside a loop cannot be carried into the loop (GB018), only one can be passed to a subprogram, a WithLock region holds only the lock's record, and nesting the nil check of a subprogram's unchecked argument is GB001<br>timer ops combined with two borrows are in neither testdata nor the differential. The twoborrow differential is a single-thread test run — multi-CPU concurrency covers only the AtomicAdd counts of two borrows (no counts lost), and mixing in non-atomic stores is covered only by the GB028 rule |
| G35 | "Tracing hooks" | **loading an object with a tracepoint program needs root** (the tpfield check reads the tracefs format — for a non-root loader it is Unknown and the whole Load stops). To use raw_tp, kretprobe or uretprobe as non-root, put them in a package separate from the tracepoint<br>tracepoint fields are 8- to 64-bit integers only (arrays and `__data_loc` strings cannot be read). kretprobe / uretprobe return types are 32 / 64 bits only (read an 8 / 16-bit return value as 32 bits and convert)<br>C++ uretprobe targets, and a tool that generates tracepoint declarations, do not exist |
| G36 | "Socket and cgroup" | the differential hooks are sock_create, post_bind4, connect4, bind4, cgroup_skb in both directions, sock_ops and socket_filter — sock_release, post_bind6, sendmsg / recvmsg / getpeername / getsockname and the inet6 hooks go only as far as generation and ebpf-compile<br>the effect of sock_ops SetReply is not observed (only that the verifier accepts the write — load and attach on 3 kernels). egress _cn (2 / 3), the truncation length of socket_filter, and the unix hooks are out of scope (no demand)<br>non-root covers load, attach and socket_filter (moving a child process into the test cgroup needs root) — loading the object needs CAP_BPF + CAP_NET_ADMIN (or CAP_SYS_ADMIN) (measured on 7.1.8 only) |
| G37 | "Local storage maps" | **inode_storage is excluded** — the kernel gives the inode_storage helpers only to lsm programs (the 7.1.8 verifier: `program of this type cannot use helper bpf_inode_storage_get#145`; the 6.12 / 6.6 VM kernels lack the map type). Generation and ebpf-compile only<br>**cgrp_storage on 7.1.8 / 6.12 only** — the owner cgroup comes from the pointer argument of tp_btf cgroup_mkdir, so on 6.6 gobpf.Load's arg_nullable stops it (an expected refusal — not counted as measured). task / sk use a fentry owner on 3 kernels<br>NoCreate runs on a real kernel only for sk (task / cgrp go only as far as generation and compile); non-root on 7.1.8 only |
| G38 | "kprobe" | only as a top-level statement of the program body (inside if / loop / subprogram is GB008 — to be widened on request). Plain x86_64 kprobes only (no reads through uprobe or kprobe_multi arguments)<br>the target's layout and address space are not checked (the user writes off and T from the kernel struct — the ptr declaration only says that the target argument is a pointer). Measured: offsets 0 / 8 with a width of 8 bytes, NULL and a user address (the value cells on 3 kernels are openat2's open_how; the NULL status on the host only)<br>non-root on 7.1.8 only |
| G39 | "tp_btf and CO-RE" | only as a top-level statement of the program body (as with TPArgInt). A kernel char is unsigned (uint8) — sign and width mismatches are stopped by gobpf.Load's farg (confirmed as root on 3 kernels — a non-root CheckTarget gets EPERM from the program type probe and never reaches farg)<br>the measured values are the fixed values of the tracing test run (test1 to test6 — small positive values only; negative values and high bits are not measured)<br>non-root on 7.1.8 only |
| G40 | "lsm" | **the link applies system-wide** — it attaches to the hook of every process (filtering is the author's responsibility — the differential denies only AF_XDP of the test's tgid)<br>the differential hooks are socket_create (lsm and lsm.s) and socket_post_create (lsm — struct socket's type) only. ## Out of scope

### Capabilities bpf-mlir has that gobpf does not accept (or accepts only in part)

| bpf-mlir feature path | Capability | gobpf |
|---|---|---|
| F10 | packet.load that returns 0 out of range | intentionally absent — range-checked windows only |
| F29 | once reads and writes of shared memory | absent |

### Outside the Go subset (the capability table — GB011 when used in an eBPF-side function)

| Capability | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `go.chan` | channel operations |
| `go.defer` | defer |
| `go.float` | floating point |
| `go.goroutine` | go statements |
| `go.heap` | heap allocation (taking an address with &, composite literals, new / make / append) |
| `go.interface` | dynamic interface calls |
| `go.map` | Go maps |
| `go.panic` | panic / recover |
| `go.runtime` | calls to Go runtime functions |
| `go.slice` | slice |
| `go.string` | string |
| `go.unbounded_loop` | loops not in a bounded form |
| `unknown` | constructs not in the capability table (fail closed) |
